comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Decided: (a) is the ask, (b) is the build, and they are not
alternatives.** Raise the upstream card, then build without waiting for
it.

**The expensive part is neither of them.** The find bar, choosing scope,
landing on a hit and scrolling the pane to it are the same code whether
the regex runs in herdr or in the core. Only the matcher differs, and it
is one function - `find(pane, needle) -> hits`. Build behind that seam
over `pane.read`, and swap the implementation if herdr gains search.

So the upstream card carries **both** asks, a search method and the read
cap, since (b) needs the cap lifted anyway and it is the smaller and more
likely-granted of the two.

**Take (c) for the one thing it is good at.** After the core has found a
hit and scrolled it into view, libghostty's `search:<text>` highlights
what is now on screen. It already draws the highlight and Muster already
drives libghostty actions by string name. Core finds and navigates; the
renderer draws. That is a division of labour rather than a second
matcher - there is still exactly one answer to "how many hits are there",
and it comes from the core.

**Borrow Ghostty's find bar itself.** Ghostty is MIT and checked out
locally, and the widget in it is the one we want. Three facts for
whoever picks this up:

- **It is not in libghostty.** `SurfaceSearchOverlay` is SwiftUI in
  Ghostty's macOS app - `macos/Sources/Ghostty/Surface View/SurfaceView.swift`,
  roughly lines 369-584 at our pinned 9f9b8d1d0 - plus
  `BackportSelectionTextField` from `macos/Sources/Helpers/Backport.swift`.
  This is copying Swift source, not calling a library function.
- **It separates cleanly.** Its only ties to Ghostty are `surfaceView` and
  a `SearchState` observable holding needle text, selection, total and
  selected index. Both are ours to substitute. Drag-to-reposition comes
  along for free.
- **MIT means keeping the notice**: `Copyright (c) 2024 Mitchell
  Hashimoto, Ghostty contributors`. A header on the borrowed file plus a
  third-party notice somewhere findable, which we want anyway the first
  time we vendor anything else.

**Cost to name: this brings SwiftUI into the shell.** `Sources/` has no
`import SwiftUI` and no `NSHostingView` today. SwiftUI is a system
framework rather than a new dependency, and one hosted overlay is
contained, but the shell is meant to be thin and per-OS - so the rule
ships with the borrow: SwiftUI stays inside this overlay.

**Scope: the focused pane first.** Find across every pane the window
holds is the better feature and the shape of this product, but it is a
follow-on once the matcher is cheap, not the first version.

**While the read cap exists the UI says what it searched.** A find bar
that has to explain its own reach is awkward, and it is still better than
a confident "no results" covering four fifths of a pane's history. It
stops being awkward when the cap lifts.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Measured before building** - `corpus/herdr-0.8.0/read-depth/`, `docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md` section 17 and `libghostty-9f9b8d1d.md` section 10. Upstream card raised as a_29Ayr1P8F, carrying both asks.

Three things the measurement settles, one of which was the risk this feature rested on.

**A read's lines are grid rows, exactly.** `pane.read --source recent` ends with the rows `--source visible` returns, and scrolling up a hundred rows put exactly the hundred-rows-earlier slice of that read on screen. So a match's line index converts to an `offset_from_bottom` with no correction, and landing on a hit is arithmetic. Had this gone the other way, (b) was not buildable and the whole card was blocked on the upstream.

**The cap is a thousand rows and it is silent.** 1001, 2000 and 100000 all returned 1000 rows of a pane holding 2978, and an `offset` key sent anyway succeeded while being ignored. `truncated` does come back and means "there is more than this" rather than "you hit the ceiling" - which is the flag the find bar needs, and not a way to detect the clamp.

**`recent` and `recent_unwrapped` are a real choice, not a preference.** A 167-character line came back from the first as the five rows it occupies and from the second as one line of 167. Positions are computable in one and needles crossing a wrap match in the other; there is no source that is both, and reading both would give two answers to how many matches there are. Taking `recent`, since a hit nobody can scroll to is worse than a hit that was never found.

Also worth recording against option (c): libghostty's search covers a full scrollback and runs on its own thread, which sounds better than it is here - a pane's surface is repainted from herdr's frames and keeps no history, so that engine would be searching one screen. It stays a highlighter, as decided. Its matcher is `std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase`, so the core's has to be plain ASCII case-insensitive substring or the counter disagrees with the highlight under it.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
⌘F, the way Ghostty ships it. The good half is that libghostty already
does the work; the hard half is that in Muster it would be searching the
wrong buffer.

**libghostty at our pinned commit (9f9b8d1d0) already has search.** The
bindings are there - `search:<text>`, `search_selection`,
`navigate_search`, `start_search`, `end_search` - and so are the four
actions it reports back: `START_SEARCH` carrying the needle,
`END_SEARCH`, `SEARCH_TOTAL` and `SEARCH_SELECTED`. Muster already drives
libghostty actions by string name for font sizing, so the door is open
and the wiring is small.

**But surfaces hold no scrollback, and that is deliberate**
(architecture.md: "a frame stream has no history, so surfaces hold no
scrollback and never handle the wheel"). Ghostty's find searches a buffer
Ghostty owns. Muster's surface is a viewport the daemon repaints, so
lifting the implementation gives a find that searches roughly one screen
and says "no results" for text three pages up. That is worse than having
no find at all, because it answers confidently.

**The daemon owns the history and cannot search it either.** Measured on
the pinned herdr 0.8.0:

- No search method exists. `pane.read` and the `pane.output_matched`
  event are the whole surface area.
- `pane.read` is capped in practice. A pane whose own
  `scroll.max_offset_from_bottom` reported **4981** lines returned **998**
  lines to `--source recent --lines 2000` and the same 998 to
  `--lines 100000`.

So a core-side find built on `pane.read` today would silently miss four
fifths of that pane's history - the same confident wrong answer, one
layer up.

Where find runs is therefore the decision, and it wants making before any
code:

- **(a) Ask herdr for search.** Fits view = f(daemon state), and it is
  the only option that makes the interesting version possible: find
  across every pane the window holds, including the ones no region is
  showing. That is a much better feature than find-in-this-pane, and it
  is the shape of this product - the sidebar already exists to reach work
  that is not on screen. Costs an upstream dependency. Probably wants its
  own 🔌 Upstream card.
- **(b) Core-side over `pane.read`,** which needs the read cap lifted -
  a smaller upstream ask - and then Muster matches, and lands on a hit by
  sending a scroll intent. More code here, less waiting on somebody else.
- **(c) Surface-side via libghostty, scoped honestly to what is on
  screen.** Cheap, instant, already highlights, and available today. Only
  acceptable if the UI says that is what it searched, which is a strange
  thing to have to say in a find bar.

Lean: (c) alone is not worth shipping, and (a) is the version worth
wanting. Worth asking herdr what it thinks before choosing - and worth
noticing that a hybrid of (c) for the visible screen and (a) or (b) for
the rest means one result list with two sources, which is the kind of
thing that disagrees at exactly the wrong moment.

**What is liftable regardless of the answer**: the interaction. Ghostty's
find bar, ⌘F to open, next/previous, escape to end, and a
"3 of 47" counter fed by `SEARCH_TOTAL` and `SEARCH_SELECTED`. That also
needs a text field, which Muster does not have anywhere yet - shared with
a_2936QHMRa (custom names), and the two should agree on what a text input
looks like here rather than inventing one each.
title: 🔎 Find in a pane, when the pane's history is somewhere else
